title: "Save Me, O God, the Swelling Floods
description: "Save Me, O God, the Swelling Floods in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 12 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 69, part 1, headed “The sufferings of Christ for our salvation”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Save me, O God, the swel-ling floods "Break in up-on my soul: "I sink, and sor-rows o'er my head "Like might-y wa-ters roll.

lines: "Save me, O God, the swelling floods
"I sink, and sorrows o'er my head
"I cry till all my voice be gone,
"They hate my soul without a cause,
"More than the hairs around my head,
"'Twas then I paid that dreadful debt
"And gave those honours to thy law
Thus in the great Messiah's name,
Thus he awakes our hearts to grief,
And gives us joy by turns.
"Now shall the saints rejoice and find
"For I have borne their heavy load
"Grief, like a garment, cloth'd me round,
"And bore their vile reproach to bring
"Yet when I cleans'd my father's house
"He sav'd me from the dreadful deep,
"He rais'd and fix'd my sinking feet
"And for my sake my God shall hear

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
